Could you give some more details what the actual problem is and how you tried to solve it?

@normanmaurer The issue is that the OpenSSLEngine impl assumed in its unwrap call that "src" contained a single, valid TLS record. So it asserts that the record must be less than the maximum record size but does no further validation or error checking. That record is then copied into a temporary buffer and read into OpenSSL where any validation occurs.

The java SSLEngine impl allows "src" to contain multiple TLS records but only decodes one for every call to unwrap. So it parses the header to validate the record before decryption.

The change to Netty changed the SSLHandler behavior to call unwrap with multiple records aggregated into a single buffer instead of just one record. Sometimes the aggregated records exceeded the length of the maximum allowed record size, causing OpenSSLEngine to throw an exception.

I've tried to do two different things here, the first is to emulate the java SSLEngine by having OpenSSLEngine decode the packet length and only write one packet at a time to OpenSSL for each call to unwrap. This was unacceptably slow :(

I then tried to accumulate as many packets in "src" that would fit into a max record size buffer and write the accumulated packets into OpenSSL at the same time. This too was unacceptably slow :(

@jpinner couldnt we just set the position and limit on the ByteBuffer before pass it over?
